articles.title: DRDO invites Bids for S-Band High Power Microwave Development
articles.text:
DRDO has issued RFP (Request for Proposal) under its Project SHIELD under Tender (DTDF/06/13918,) seeking to develop an S-band High Power Microwave Integrated Evaluation System , to be built under the Technology Development Fund scheme.
The RFP calls for a modular, scalable system based on Gallium Nitride solid-state power amplifier technology, a more compact and efficient approach than the venerable (and bulky) vacuum tube magnetrons and klystrons used in earlier high-power microwave systems.
The DRDO seeks a peak electric field strength of at least 3 kV/m in the far field, in a pulsed mode with variable duty cycles to allow researchers to model a range of attack profiles, not just a single waveform. Meanwhile, systems operating at these power levels produce significant waste heat, requiring advanced thermal management techniques built into the design.
The S-band spans 2 to 4 gigahertz, a busy spectrum encompassing home Wi-Fi, some satellite links, airport radars, and the control links of cheap commercial drones, among other things. The fact that military systems operate in the same space makes these systems vulnerable to being targeted and jammed by an adversary’s drone or radar, and DRDO wants a proper evaluation platform in order to properly assess a future weapon system’s capabilities.
High-Power Microwave (HPM) technologies are a form of directed-energy weapons (DEW), which differ from laser beams in that, rather than using a narrow beam of concentrated light to burn through a target, HPMs generate powerful pulses of microwave radiation that can disrupt and destroy electronics and digital circuitry by firing broad, conical beams of radiofrequency energy at them.
Since drone swarms depend largely on interconnected commercial electronics and GPS/RF tracking, a single broad-sweeping HPM burst could burn up the speed controllers and microcontrollers of dozens of incoming drones at once, causing them to plummet to earth.
Microwave tube Research and Development Centre in Bengaluru have already developed, tested, and deployed a ground-based S-band HPM directed energy weapon capable of taking out drone swarms and have a range of about a kilometer against small quadcopters and hopes to extend it to five kilometers. SHIELD seems to the next logical step, providing the infrastructure for thorough characterization of lethality and damage before such kind of weapons can be serialised.

articles.title: HAL Seeks Indian Industry Partners to Manufacture and Supply Shakti Helicopter Engine Reduction Gear Modules
articles.text:
HAL has issued an Expression of Interest (EOI) seeking Indian industry participation for the detail-parts manufacturing, assembly and supply of the Reduction Gear Module of the Shakti engine. The tender is identified as HAL-ADL/CWA-26AC/3. EOI for Detail Parts Manufacturing, Assembly and Supply of Reduction Gear Module of Shakti Engine.
The Shakti is the HAL-produced/licensed version of the Safran Helicopter Engines Ardiden 1H1 family and powers major Indian military helicopters including the Dhruv ALH, Rudra and Light Combat Helicopter (LCH). HAL is not asking for a spare component. It is seeking industry participation for Detail-parts manufacturing → assembly → complete Reduction Gear Module supply.
A turboshaft engine produces power at extremely high rotational speed. The helicopter’s main rotor requires a much lower rotational speed and considerable torque. The reduction gearbox/module performs this speed reduction while transmitting engine power to the helicopter’s drivetrain. So this is a high-value rotating aerospace component, involving precision gears, shafts, bearings, housings, lubrication and high-speed/high-load operation.
The tender is being issued by HAL’s Accessories Division/engine-related industrial organisation in Lucknow, not a generic helicopter spare procurement. The tender number HAL-ADL/CWA-26AC/3 is particularly useful for tracking subsequent corrigenda, vendor-selection announcements and eventual contract awards.
HAL has historically manufactured and overhauled Shakti engines in India, but the new EOI specifically seeks external industry participation for the detail parts, assembly and supply of the reduction gear module.
Edited by Raunak Kunde

articles.title: Russian Plans to sell 200 MC-21 Aircrafts to Indian Operators
articles.text:
Russia is discussing the potential sale of more than 200 jetliners of the MS-21 type with India’s commercial organizations. This information was reported by the news agency TASS, quoting Sberbank First Deputy Chairman of the Management Board Alexander Vedyakhin. HAL has officially confirmed that an MoU was signed with Russia’s United Aircraft Corporation (UAC) for the production of the SJ-100 on October 27, 2025.
HAL is interested in selling the Russian MC-21 regional aircraft to India. The Russian aircraft will initially be provided on a lease basis, and later, their assembly will begin in India. In addition, if the orders arrive, then their full copy will also be produced on the territory of this country, said a representative of HAL at the time of the deal with Russia’s UAC.
“HAL is interested in promoting the MC-21 aircraft in the Indian market. The response was enthusiastic, although the estimates were different. For example, UAC expects an order of 100-200 planes from Indian airlines. We will do our best to help our Russian colleagues fulfill their plans,” said Alexander Vedyakhin.
It is also known that Aeroflot has signed an option for the purchase of 18 MC-21 aircraft. It was reported in August that Aeroflot plans to sign a supplemental agreement with UAC to buy 90 more planes.
Thus, UAC is looking to sell the MC-21 medium-haul aircraft to India. At the same time, its representatives are also considering the possibility of manufacturing these planes in India. However, so far, none of India’s airlines have shown any interest in buying the MC-21. On Wings India 2026, UAC CEO Vadim Badekha said that they are considering the prospect of the Indian market for the MC-21 aircraft. “They are looking at the option of manufacturing and selling them in India. However, so far, no Indian airline has announced the purchase of aircraft,” he noted.
Edited by Raunak Kunde
articles.summary: Russia is discussing the potential sale of more than 200 jetliners of the MS-21 type with India’s commercial organizations. This information was reported by the news agency TASS, quoting Sberbank Firs

articles.title: Taiwan Media Praises rise of ” BrahMos Belt ” against China in South-East Asian Countries
articles.text:
Taiwan Talks recently hosted a retired Indian Army General P.R. Shankar (retired), who was responsible for BrahMos induction and upgrades. The episode discusses the missile’s combat use and export, with an emphasis on its low cost per unit and increasing international sales. The underlying theme is the informal “BrahMos Belt” (missile ring/wall) being formed by the presence of shore-based batteries in the Philippines, Vietnam, and Indonesia (with Thailand considering the purchase).
They are all situated in such a way as to extend coverage over critical South China Sea areas, including Luzon/Bashi Strait, and the Malacca Strait. Analysts believe that this will greatly complicate Chinese operations in the region without necessarily entering into any open alliances. The batteries in the Philippines are already positioned to cover critical areas in the northern Luzon in case of a Taiwan contingency.
BrahMos is a joint Indo-Russian venture, which flies at about Mach 2.8-3, with low radar cross-section, and can skim the waves at high speed, making it very hard to shoot down. The export versions have a maximum range of about 290 km (under MTCR guidelines), while India possesses further improved missiles. The Philippines is the first country to buy the missile (a contract was signed in 2022, with deliveries beginning in 2024), followed by Vietnam (likely to sign the contract soon) and Indonesia. All these countries have maritime disputes with China, so it is not surprising that they are interested in acquiring BrahMos.
The analysts then turn to the Indo-Pacific balance and whether this will affect the security situation in the Taiwan Strait. India does not sell defense equipment to Taiwan due to its One China policy, as well as to not offend Russia, despite growing economic and technological ties with the ROC. Overall, Taiwan Talks highlights the BrahMos missile’s unique characteristics and how its sales to the Philippines, Vietnam, Indonesia, and potentially Thailand and Malaysia, will impact the regional security situation.
Its coverage capabilities, when combined with other anti-ship systems and missiles, will greatly challenge Chinese naval operations in the South China Sea and adjacent waters, while not requiring these countries to build up their military capabilities to the same level as China.
However, how much this will affect Beijing’s plans to establish naval supremacy depends on how many batteries will be deployed in these countries, how prepared their crews will be, how much targeting information will be available to them during a contingency, and how willing they will be to directly oppose China.

articles.title: India Needs Its Own Carl-Gustaf M4 — Can Private Defence Firms Deliver?
articles.text:
There is a strategic and commercial case for Indian private companies to develop Carl-Gustaf M4-class infantry weapons, rather than simply acquiring another foreign OEM’s product. The aim should be a domestic equivalent that offers weight savings, common ammunition, improved sighting systems, and lifecycle economics.
The Indian Army has a vast infantry presence, representing a huge demand for shoulder-fired, anti-armour, and multipurpose weapons. A successful, indigenously developed weapon would find a substantial market beyond an initial order by the Army. An Indian private company developing a lightweight recoilless weapon could target Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Latin America—regions where many nations require budget-friendly infantry firepower.
The launcher itself is just one element in the system. The development of a Carl-Gustaf-class weapon would spur Indian industry to create a range of 84mm-class or equivalent ammunition, including anti-armor, bunker-busting, smoke, and illuminating rounds. India does not necessarily need to copy the Carl-Gustaf design.
A private-sector project could aim for a lighter composite launcher, enhanced thermal sights, digital fire-control systems, programmable ammunition, and improved ergonomics. Such projects could involve Indian companies in advanced manufacturing processes such as carbon-fiber composites, machining, optics, electronics, and propulsion technologies. The greatest strategic benefit would be assured supply security.
A domestic design would give the Army greater control over production, ammunition availability, upgrades, and spares in a prolonged conflict. The Carl-Gustaf M4 should not be seen simply as a foreign weapon India acquires, but rather as a technology benchmark.

articles.title: Arjun MBT Rolls Into War Thunder’s Sky Odyssey Update
articles.text:
Indian defence gaming fans have reason to rejoice this week, as Gaijin Entertainment’s War Thunder first showcased India’s indigenously-developed Arjun Main Battle Tank in the game as a part of its next major update called Sky Odyssey, revealed this September 3. This update is likely to be welcomed with open arms by the Indian gaming community which has long desired to see India’s achievements in military technology recognised and celebrated.
In Past, War Thunder featured several unique Indian military vehicles like MiG-21 Bison and the Vijayanta tank both that have been retired and not in service anymore.
Indian gamers have been demanding incursion of many Indian weapons system like HAL Marut, HAL Ajeet, and the LCH Prachand helicopters and their is high demand also for incursion of Tejas Mk1A in the Game. Latest update also features Chinese J-16 aircraft that is based on the Russian Su-27KUB and also has various Chinese air defence system that was previous not in the game,
A list of the tanks to be featured in the update has not yet been released by Gaijin Entertainment, with the company providing no information about specific configurations, battle rating, or the Mk1/Mk2 of the tank that will enter the game. The details are likely to become more clear as the release date of the update approaches, as it has been a common practice for War Thunder to reveal some details in the trailers, but not all of them. It is still uncertain whether it will enter as a standalone branch or be integrated into an existing tech tree.
Edited by Raunak Kunde

articles.title: Indian Army Inducts Indigenous Ice Axes and Shovels
articles.text:
An Indian company, MSA, has declared that its home-grown ice axes and shovels have been accepted into service by the Indian Army for use in extreme weather conditions. MSA says its first lot of ice axes and shovels have been accepted into service by the Indian Army. The company says it is a historic first as it is the first Indian-made ice axe and shovel that has been accepted for use in such extreme conditions. The equipment has been engineered for use in extreme cold conditions as per MSA, who say it can withstand temperatures down to -50C.
The products are said to be resistant to breakage and corrosion while being kept to a total weight of less than 1.4 kg. Lightweight, yet strong, is a crucial requirement for soldiers to carry kit at high altitudes as every extra kg adds to a soldier’s burden. MSA states that the products went through extensive development before being accepted by the Army.
The design and prototyping phase reportedly took around 16 months, followed by about three years of field testing. The company then went from the development stage to mass manufacturing in just six months.
The long field-testing period enabled the equipment to be tested under tough operating conditions before moving to full-scale production. The bulk-produced ice axes then went through over 150 additional tests before being accepted into service, according to MSA.
These included functional, load, strength, mechanical and chemical testing at NABL-accredited laboratories. Such testing is vital to equipment for use in extreme environments, where failure of materials can put soldiers’ lives at risk.
Specialised individual equipment and extreme-weather kit are also essential for troops operating in hostile environments. Developing such products domestically will enable the armed forces to gain greater control over the design, supply and future modification of the equipment.
Edited by Raunak Kunde

articles.title: IAF’s Dornier-228 Fleet does Elephant Walk
articles.text:
The Indian Air Force (IAF) has presented the combat-readiness of its Do-228 aircraft fleet during an impressive “Elephant Walk” at Air Force Station Yelahanka in Bengaluru.
The demonstration served to showcase the size of the fleet as well as the maintenance, coordination and crews’ proficiency in operating it, needed to ensure each aircraft is ready for immediate take-off.
An Elephant Walk is a formation march usually made up of multiple planes which taxi together before take-off. Such displays are made to show off the military’s might, aircraft’s combat-readiness and ability to perform coordinated actions. They also highlight the importance of maintenance in keeping aircraft operational. The ability to keep a fleet of aircraft ready to roll is the result of the close cooperation between mechanics, ground crews, pilots, and other personnel.
For the IAF, the display was an opportunity to demonstrate the combat-readiness of its transport aircraft fleet.
The crew proficiency is of particular importance for utility aircraft, which are highly versatile but have to be able to operate from a variety of take-off and landing strips. The Dornier Do-228 has been a mainstay of India’s military and government aviation for decades, serving in numerous roles as a transport aircraft. The IAF’s presentation, which was accompanied by the slogan “Balamcha Budhischa”, highlighted the power and wisdom required to employ these aircraft and turn them into formidable instruments of war.

articles.title: Adani Defence, Indo-Russian Rifles Sign Five-Year Ammunition Supply Pact for AK-203
articles.text:
Adani Defence & Aerospace has signed a five-year agreement with Indo-Russian Rifles Private Limited (IRRPL), the India-Russia joint venture manufacturing AK-203 assault rifles in India, to supply indigenous 7.62×39 mm small-calibre ammunition for the programme.
The agreement brings together AK-203 rifle production by IRRPL and ammunition production by Adani Defence & Aerospace, creating an integrated supply chain in India. Under the agreement, Adani Defence & Aerospace will supply 7.62×39 mm ammunition for the AK-203 for five years. The arrangement provides an Indian source for the ammunition required for the programme and supports continuity of supply during the contract period.
IRRPL was incorporated in 2019 under an India-Russia intergovernmental agreement to manufacture AK-203 assault rifles for the Indian Armed Forces. Its manufacturing facility is located at Korwa in Amethi district, Uttar Pradesh. The joint venture has Indian shareholders Advanced Weapons and Equipment India Limited and Munitions India Limited, along with Russian shareholders Concern Kalashnikov and Rosoboronexport.
The Ministry of Defence has identified IRRPL as the joint venture established for indigenous production of the AK-203. A contract for 6,01,427 AK-203 rifles was signed with IRRPL in December 2021, with the rifles to be produced at Korwa. Adani Defence & Aerospace has established manufacturing capabilities for small-calibre ammunition in India, including a facility in Kanpur with production capacity for small-calibre ammunition.
The agreement further strengthens domestic capabilities across the small-arms supply chain and supports the Aatmanirbhar Bharat objective in defence manufacturing.

articles.title: HSL Lays Keel for Second 60 Ton Bollard Pull Tug for VPA
articles.text:
Hindustan Shipyard Limited today laid the keel of the second 60 Ton Bollard Pull Tug, VC 11206, for Visakhapatnam Port Authority (VPA), performed by Chief Guest Shri Jasmeet Singh Bindra, IRTS, Chairperson, VPA, in the presence of senior officials from VPA, HSL, IRS and Solas Marine. Contracted in Dec 2025 and built to IRS class, its twin tug has crossed 60% completion, with both set to float out together this October. This is HSL’s 13th vessel for VPA since Launch Shanti in 1970.
Chief Guest Shri Jasmeet Singh Bindra said the two tugs are strategic assets that will strengthen safe berthing and cut turnaround time at the port, reflecting HSL’s renewed momentum under Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat. He called VPA and HSL two heritage organisations of Vizag, both serving the nation for over 90 years, commending HSL for holding its timelines, from steel cutting in February to keel laying today.
RAdm Chandrasekharan Raghuram, VSM (Retd.), C&MD, HSL, thanking Shri Bindra, VPA’s officials, IRS, and HSL’s officers, supervisors and workmen, said HSL remains committed to delivering on its word. He outlined a far larger partnership taking shape with VPA, including a proposed 60 ton electric tug and green fleet conversion, a long term ship repair tie up using HSL’s dry dock, and a future shipbuilding complex at Dugarajapatnam. “One yard, one mission, powering India’s maritime destiny,” he said.
Together, HSL and VPA are building more than tugs, a partnership aligned with Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat 2047, positioning Visakhapatnam as a major shipbuilding and maritime hub.

articles.title: French Navy frigate Languedoc completes port call in Goa
articles.text:
French Navy’s multi-mission frigate ‘Languedoc’ completed a scheduled operational stop at the port of Mormugao in Goa on Friday after a four-day visit aimed at strengthening maritime cooperation between India and France, the French Embassy said.
The FREMM-class frigate, deployed on a mission in the Red Sea and Indian Ocean, is undertaking surveillance, situation assessment and protection duties in the maritime region, the embassy said in a press release.
The vessel was in Goa from August 31 to September 4. The Indian Navy welcomed the vessel and its crew, with an official lunch attended by Commodore L M Fernandes, Deputy Commander of the Goa Naval Area, and Agnes Silva, Deputy Consul of France in Mumbai, it said.
The port call also included a visit by a French-speaking class from the Navy Children School in Goa, giving the students an opportunity to see life aboard a modern French combat vessel, the embassy said.
French and Indian sailors also exchanged expertise in areas including logistics of deployed units, anti-drone warfare and underwater diving, it said.
The visit marks the third visit to India by a French naval vessel this year and underlines France’s continued naval presence and commitment to maritime security in the Indian Ocean Region, the embassy said.
The two navies are scheduled to meet again later this month in the Mediterranean Sea near Toulon for VARUNA 2026, the annual Indo-French bilateral naval exercise, it added.

articles.title: AI sovereignty crucial for cybersecurity, says Gaganyaan astronaut
articles.text:
Gaganyaan astronaut and IAF pilot Prasanth Balakrishnan Nair on Saturday said AI sovereignty is crucial for ensuring national cybersecurity, as the growing use of artificial intelligence is making it increasingly difficult to distinguish between real and fake content.
Speaking at the Kerala Cyber Suraksha Summit 2026, organised by Kerala Startup Mission and F9 Infotech, Nair said cybersecurity would have limited value unless the country developed ownership and control over AI technologies.
“It is very important that we have AI sovereignty, and any amount of cybersecurity will be of no avail unless we own AI,” he said.
Nair said future wars and industries would involve a “whole-of-nation approach”, making it increasingly difficult to distinguish between physical and digital boundaries. “In the whole-of-nation approach, it’s very difficult to say where the physical boundaries end and where the digital boundaries start. And it’s going to affect all of us,” he said.
He stressed the need for greater awareness of cybersecurity and digital threats as AI, cyber technology and the digital environment become increasingly integrated into everyday life.
“We are all using digital and now AI is coming. We forget which is real and which is fake. It’s important to make sure that we, like in the olden days, keep our stuff inside the vault and lock it. We have to make sure that digitally we are secure,” he said.
Nair said India has demonstrated its technological capabilities through the successful Chandrayaan-3 mission, which landed near the Moon’s south polar region in August 2023.
“Remember that we all are Indians and we have that power. We are the ones who on 23 August 2023 put Chandrayaan-3 on the South Pole of the Moon, which nobody else has done,” he said.
He also noted India’s significant contribution to the global software ecosystem and said the country needed to build on these capabilities in AI, cybersecurity and digital technology.
“What we need right now is to understand that AI, cyber and digital environment is here to stay. It’s going to affect all our countrymen, and there are no exact boundaries,” Nair said. He said space technology itself demonstrated how interconnected the physical and digital worlds have become and called for responsible use of AI to improve people’s lives.
Vinayak Godse, CEO of the Data Security Council of India, said Keralam had significant potential to contribute to national, industrial and global technology requirements.
“We believe Keralam has a lot of potential. There is a lot of good talent available here. The basic literacy is very significantly higher here,” Godse said.
He said Keralam could develop and deliver solutions needed at the national, industrial and global levels, adding that it remained to be seen how the state’s technology ecosystem can evolve to achieve those objectives.
“We’d like to see that progress happening,” he said.
DGP Manoj Abraham said cyberattacks could now cripple nations and organisations, disable critical infrastructure and disrupt military operations without a single shot being fired.
“There has been a 389 per cent rise in ransomware victims worldwide, year-over-year, and in India the reported financial losses owing to cyber fraud in 2025 alone were worth Rs 19,813 crore. We are at a juncture where we need more defenders to take on the cyber attackers. Worldwide, there are 4.8 million unfilled cybersecurity jobs,” he said.
The summit was supported by the Data Security Council of India, TiE Kerala and the Cochin Chamber of Commerce and Industry.

articles.title: India votes in favour of UNGA resolution endorsing new world map
articles.text:
India has voted in favour of a UN General Assembly resolution aimed at correcting the world map to promote a “more accurate representation” of continental landmasses.
The 193-member UN General Assembly on Friday overwhelmingly adopted the resolution ‘“Correct the map”: rebalancing global cartographic representation and promoting equitable representation of the world’s regions, particularly Africa’.
The resolution was sponsored by Togo, receiving 164 votes in favour, with abstentions from Estonia, Georgia, Lithuania, Moldova, Serbia and Ukraine, and a lone vote against from the United States.
The resolution noted that the Mercator projection, designed in the 16th century for navigational purposes, remains widely used in educational, media, digital and official materials, despite the considerable distortion of landmasses to the North and South, far from the equator.
The resolution also noted with “concern” that “this distortion contributes to minimising the perceived sizes of Africa, Latin America and South Asia, and perpetuating an unbalanced view of the world.”
In an explanation of the vote in the General Assembly, First Secretary at the Permanent Mission of India to the UN, Raghoo Puri, said India “welcomes” the intention behind the resolution to promote more accurate and representative cartographic practices.
“We believe that maps play an important role in how societies understand geography and the relative scale of the world around us,” he said. However, India clarified its understanding of the scope of this resolution, saying, “We believe that the resolution should be understood as supporting the broader use and consideration of Equal Area map projections, and not as endorsing the Equal Earth projection or any other specific map projection.”

India has voted in favour of a UN General Assembly resolution aimed at correcting the world map to promote a “more accurate representation” of continental landmasses.

articles.title: Dixon Technologies eyes foray into aerospace, defence, medical electronics
articles.text:
Dixon Technologies (India) Ltd is looking to enter high-value product segments in aerospace, defence, automotive, medical and industrial verticals as part of its next phase of growth, the company’s Director and Chief Financial Officer Saurabh Gupta said in his message to shareholders in the annual report for FY26.
Gupta said the electronics manufacturer is “identifying high-growth, high-value product opportunities” across these verticals, and is defining a capability roadmap and execution framework spanning capital allocation, talent development and strategic partnerships to accelerate Dixon’s evolution into what he called “a globally competitive manufacturing platform”.
As Dixon enters 2026-27, its priorities “remain consistent”, the CFO said: scaling backward integration investments to full production, deepening its joint venture pipeline in IT hardware, telecom and mobiles, and growing exports.
Gupta said the phased ramp-up of the company’s display and camera module facilities is expected to support a gradual improvement in margins. Dixon’s camera module business, run through its 51 per cent stake in Kunshan Q-Tech India, is targeting a scale-up in capacity from 70 million units currently to 180-190 million units over the next few years, he said.
The company is also pursuing a proposed 60:40 joint venture with Taiwan’s Gemtek Technology to manufacture optical transceivers and is moving beyond traditional end-client computing to tap into the high-growth enterprise server and data centre hardware ecosystem, and address rising cloud and artificial intelligence infrastructure demand.
Gupta said Dixon is working to transform itself into “an engineering powerhouse” aligned with the needs of global customers who increasingly seek partners capable of delivering end-to-end solutions spanning product design, engineering, manufacturing and lifecycle support.
“The company remains focused on strengthening its engineering capabilities across product architecture, component localisation, process automation, smart manufacturing, and new technology development. This strategic shift will enable Dixon to deliver higher-value solutions, accelerate innovation cycles, improve product quality and create differentiated offerings for both global and domestic brands,” he said.

articles.title: Tata Motors launches tender offer for Iveco Group; deal values company at €3.82 billion
articles.text: Tata Motors has launched a voluntary tender offer for all issued common shares of Italian transport vehicle maker Iveco Group at €14.1 per share, in cash, including the dividend.Tata Motors CV and Iveco Group jointly announced the offer's commencement by TML CV Holdings B.V. in an exchange filing on Saturday, September 5. The offer values Iveco at approximately €3.82 billion and is aimed at acquiring 100% of the company’s common shares and delisting it from Euronext Milan.To fund the transaction, Tata Motors CV signed a debt commitment letter with Morgan Stanley Bank, N.A., Morgan Stanley Senior Funding, Inc. and MUFG Bank, Ltd. for fully committed bridge financing.Exor, the Agnelli family-owned investment company and Iveco’s largest shareholder, has also irrevocably committed to support the transaction. Exor has tendered its 27% stake in Iveco’s common shares, representing 43.19% of the company’s voting rights.The transaction has also received the full and unanimous support and recommendation of Iveco’s board.The tender offer will open on Monday, September 7, while Iveco shareholders are scheduled to vote on the matter in October. The proposed transaction is intended to result in the acquisition of all common shares of Iveco and the subsequent delisting of the company from Euronext Milan.What did Tata Motors management say?Girish Wagh, Managing Director and CEO of Tata Motors, said the commencement of the tender offer marked an important milestone in bringing together two complementary organisations. He said the combination of their capabilities and market presence could help build a stronger and more globally competitive commercial vehicle business, while supporting investments in future technologies and creating sustainable value for stakeholders.Wagh also said Tata Motors had immense respect for Iveco’s heritage, people and brands, and looked forward to supporting the company’s continued growth. He added that Tata Motors believed the tender offer presented a compelling value proposition for Iveco shareholders and was looking forward to its successful completion.Tata Motors August salesThe move comes after Tata Motors reported a strong rise in commercial vehicle sales in August. In its monthly auto sales report, the company said total CV sales across domestic and international markets rose 49% year-on-year to 44,411 units in August 2026, compared with 29,863 units in August 2025.Tata Motors’ international commercial vehicle business recorded an even sharper increase during the month, with sales jumping 227% year-on-year to 7,792 units from 2,382 units a year earlier. This was the highest growth among the reported CV categories in percentage terms.(Disclaimer: Recommendations, suggestions, views and opinions given by the experts are their own. articles.text: Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami has announced that Hanuman Ansh, a film based on the life and teachings of spiritual leader Neem Karoli Baba, will be made tax-free in the state.Dhami watched the film at a cinema hall in Dehradun on Friday with his wife Geeta Dhami, cabinet ministers Ganesh Joshi and Pradeep Batra, and several MLAs. The film has emerged as a surprise hit at the box office this year.Dhami said films such as Hanuman Ansh play an important role in highlighting Uttarakhand’s spiritual and cultural heritage before audiences in India and abroad."Through the film, we had the opportunity to know and understand Baba Neem Karoli Maharaj Ji's penance, sacrifice, service, and his unwavering faith in Lord Hanuman. His entire life was dedicated to the service of humanity, spiritual practice, and the welfare of society," the chief minister said in a post on X."The life of Baba Neem Karoli Maharaj Ji gives us the message that devotion is not merely practice, but also the path of service, surrender, and human welfare," he added.Dhami congratulated the team behind Hanuman Ansh, calling it an "inspirational and spiritual film". He also said Kainchi Dham has emerged as a major centre of faith and reverence for devotees around the world.What is Hanuman Ansh about?Written and directed by Vishal Chaturvedi, Hanuman Ansh follows Lakshminarayan, a young man grieving the death of his mother, who embarks on a spiritual journey in search of God.Travelling across North India in search of answers to questions surrounding life, death and human suffering, Lakshminarayan eventually transforms into the revered saint Neem Karoli Baba, whose teachings on love, service and compassion influenced countless people.The film stars Shobhinaw Satya in the lead role, alongside Vihaan Shedge, Chandan K Anand, Purnima Tiwari, Anil Rastogi, Gulshan Pandey and Bhagvandas Patel.Hanuman Ansh box office performanceHanuman Ansh was released in Indian theatres on August 7. The film had a slow start, recording modest box-office collections during its first two weeks before gaining momentum through strong word-of-mouth publicity.According to trade website Sacnilk, the film has since earned Rs 97.77 crore in gross collections and Rs 82.88 crore nett at the box office.

articles.title: ITC’s tobacco business is going cheap but Kotak Institutional Equities thinks market has it wrong
articles.text: ITC’s tobacco business appears to be getting little credit from the market, with Kotak Securities’ reverse-SoTP valuation suggesting the business is valued at around 11X its one-year forward earnings.According to Kotak Securities, the implied one-year forward P/E of ITC’s tobacco business is around 11X, based on depressed FY2027-28E earnings per share compared with FY2026 levels. The brokerage said this valuation implies that the market either expects the tobacco business’ earnings to remain stagnant at low levels in perpetuity, believes the value of ITC’s non-tobacco businesses is significantly lower, or has limited appetite for the tobacco business.Kotak’s valuation assigns a 16X multiple to September 2028E earnings for the tobacco business, resulting in a 12-month fair value of Rs 194. For the non-tobacco business, it uses 30X September 2028E EBITDA to arrive at a 12-month fair value of Rs 80. The brokerage assigns another Rs 84 to ITC’s other businesses and cash.Tobacco business: What is the market pricing in?Kotak Securities believes its 16X two-year forward P/E multiple for ITC’s tobacco business is reasonable. The multiple implies 4.8% growth in free cash flow to equity (FCFE) in perpetuity assuming an 11% cost of equity, and 5.8% perpetual FCFE growth assuming a 12% cost of equity.The brokerage noted that the implied growth in net profit is similar to the PAT growth estimates for major global tobacco companies.Against this backdrop, the 11X implied P/E for ITC’s tobacco business in the reverse-SoTP valuation suggests that the market either expects earnings to stagnate at low levels in perpetuity or considers Kotak’s near-term earnings estimates for the business too aggressive. Kotak said its assumptions for the tobacco business should address the latter concern.Non-tobacco business: A high multiple, but faster growthKotak Securities acknowledged that its 30X two-year forward EV/EBITDA multiple for ITC’s non-tobacco business may appear aggressive compared with peers, particularly after the sharp derating in their multiples over the past few months.However, the brokerage expects ITC’s non-tobacco business to deliver faster profit growth than other companies. It attributes this to likely stronger growth in several key categories where ITC has lower market shares, along with the scope for margin expansion as the business scales up.Kotak expects strong growth in revenue and EBIT from the non-tobacco business over the next few years, even with only moderate expansion in its EBIT margin.Splitting ITC could unlock valueKotak Securities believes a vertical split of ITC into two separate entities, with the tobacco business housed in one and the non-tobacco businesses in another, could unlock significant value for shareholders.According to the brokerage, the tobacco entity could attract value-oriented shareholders seeking steady growth and high dividend yields. The non-tobacco entity, meanwhile, could appeal to growth investors as well as a broader pool of investors who may otherwise be deterred by ESG concerns associated with tobacco.The brokerage’s core argument is that ITC’s current valuation does not appear to fully reflect the value it assigns to the tobacco and non-tobacco businesses separately.(Disclaimer: Recommendations, suggestions, views and opinions given by the experts are their own. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)
